newsitem.title: UK: ASDA launches half-price book sale.
newsitem.headline: ASDA launches half-price book sale.

text.p: British supermarket retailer ASDA Group Plc said on Monday that it was launching the industry's biggest ever sale of books at half recommended retail levels or less.
"ASDA is reinforcing its position as Britain's best-value book retailer," a statement from the company said.
ASDA was a major player in a campaign which smashed the Net Book Agreement, which allowed publishers to set retail prices.
It has also tackled fixed prices on over-the-counter medicines and aims to cultivate an image as a consumers' champion.
ASDA said more than 400,000 books including current best sellers would be on offer at 3.99 stg, compared with cover prices of up to 15.99 stg.
"Selling the current best-sellers at half price, and top hardbacks at under four stg, is something the traditionalists will hate but our customers will love," ASDA book buyer Julian Graham-Rack said.

ASDA, which focuses on low-price and quality without diversifying as its competitors have done, last week turned in annual pre-tax profits of 353.7 million stg, up 16 percent, with sales up 9.2 percent, the strongest gain in the industry.
